item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because it explicitly implements the required Upload validation, preserves Add’s existing option-processing order, and provides clearer coverage of both non-seekable body replay and multipart encoding. Both patches share a notable contract violation: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and calls the new private add helper directly.","reasons":["B explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before multipart construction; A leaves this required behavior implicit in multipartbody.NewFile.","B keeps newFilesOptions(opts) at the start of Add, while A moves option processing until after the body has been consumed, introducing an unnecessary behavioral-order change.","B tests replay using a genuinely one-shot reader and separately verifies Upload’s method, path, multipart field, filename, content, and retry behavior with an os.File.","Both correctly reuse multipartbody.NewFile and buffer Add bodies into bytes.Reader values for retry replay."],"risks_a":["Upload calls s.add rather than routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors.","Required validation is not explicit in FilesService.Upload and depends on undocumented helper behavior in the presented material."],"risks_b":["Upload calls s.add rather than routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required, potentially diverging from Add’s error semantics later.","No visible tests cover validation or source-reader failures despite the test contract.","The combined validation error does not identify whether the filename or content was invalid."]}
